subject: Sparse representation for covariates in spatio-temporal model?

messages.author: 2261794abc623416
messages.subject: Sparse representation for covariates in spatio-temporal model?
parts:
Hi all, 

I'm a relatively new R-INLA user and hopefully there is a quick and relatively simple answer to my problem. 

I'm currently investigating disease spread, and have a spatio-temporal model similar to that proposed in equation 4 of this paper (doi:10.1111/j.1541-0420.2011.01717.x). As the number of areas in this paper is relatively small, memory usage is not of major concern. However, I have approximately 100,000 spatial areas that need to be considered. I understand I can use the generic1 option in the formula setting for the precision matrix of the spatial surface, which will undoubtedly help in this instance. I am wondering, is there a similar sparse representation that can be used for covariates? For my model in particular we have movements between the 100,000 spatial areas (100,000 x 100,000 matrix) for each year in a 10-year window, with approximately 99% of the elements in these movements matrices being 0. If I can use a sparse representation of the movements, similar to that required by the generic1 option, it will undoubtedly help the memory issues I'm encountering. 

Any help is greatly appreciated.
Aoife
